predecessors.name: Spanish Empire
predecessors.text: the Almolonga Valley around Santiago de los Caballeros de Guatemala

successors.name: First Mexican Empire
successors.text: present-day Costa Rica, Nicaragua, Honduras, El Salvador, Guatemala, and the Mexican state of Chiapas, without the Mosquito Coast strip of 1803

successors.name: Federal Republic of Central America
successors.text: the region without Chiapas, without the Mosquito Coast strip of 1803

capitals.name: Santiago de los Caballeros de Guatemala (Almolonga, now Ciudad Vieja)
Santiago de los Caballeros de Guatemala (Antigua Guatemala)

ledger.x: 1527: the Kingdom of Guatemala is established.
1543: the Audiencia of Guatemala fixes the kingdom's territory.
1609: the governor and Audiencia president also becomes captain general.
1697 (13 March): Nojpetén falls and the Petén is incorporated into the captaincy.
1776: the capital moves from Antigua to Guatemala City.
1783: Britain's logwood cutters hold ground in the Belize area under Spanish sovereignty.
1803 (20 November): a royal decree gives New Granada a strip of the Mosquito Coast.
1821: the Spanish claim over the Belize settlement ends with the captaincy.
1821 (15 September): the captaincy ends in the Act of Independence of Central America.

wars.name: Spanish-British contest for the Belize logwood coast
wars.outcome: Spain 'chased out the Baymen four times between 1717 and 1780' but conceded logwood cutting between the Hondo and Belize rivers in 1783 and to the Sibun in 1786 while keeping sovereignty; 'Spain never attempted to reclaim the area after 1798'.

certainty.note: No surveyed borders: provincial limits follow the Audiencia's jurisdiction and the Caribbean coast was never effectively held.
The Hondo, Belize and Sibun rivers are treaty lines (1783, 1786) for the logwood settlement only; all other frontiers stay soft.
